text:
Samir: Starting config deploy to canary-1 at 21:10 UTC. Only changing rate limits and batch window. No model changes. Pinned runtime=2.3.1 for canary.

deploy-bot: Deploy triggered by Samir. Change window: 21:10-21:40. Canary target: traffic=2% -> 10 instances. ID c-3178901234.

Jules: Noted. Config: rate_limit_per_user=20r/s -> 10r/s, route_penalty=0.8, batch_window_ms=12 -> 8. Also reduced kv_cache_ttl from 600s -> 300s.

Maya: Quick ask — did we update the fallback routing? If primary region degrades, will it pin to v2.3.0 or fallback to a smaller batch variant?

Samir: Fallback policy is "pin-to-stable" -> v2.3.0. I left a canary override to allow 5s extra timeout on retries. See config blob:
```
canary: { traffic: 0.02, runtime: "2.3.1", overrides: { rate_limit: 10, batch_ms: 8, fallback_policy: "pin-to-stable" } }
```

Rae: Deploy-bot metrics: canary up; initial p50 latency +3ms, p95 +18ms, error rate raw=0.02% (no spike). :thumbsup:

Jules: Observing slight tokenization CPU increase on canary nodes — may be due to tighter batching. Keeping watch.

Maya: Suggest rollforward to 10% after 10m if error rate <0.1% and p95 < +50ms. Agree?

Rae: Agreed. Also add quick smoke check: run `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST' https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"smoke"}'` on a canary node.

Samir: Doing smoke now. Response OK. No regressions in structured output.

deploy-bot: Canary traffic increased to 10% at 21:18 UTC. Rollout window ends 21:40 UTC. Monitoring: infra.alerts disabled for routine during window.

Jules: Noticing 401 spikes for a tiny subset — investigating auth proxy logs, might be stale token cache after kv_ttl change.

Maya: If 401 > 0.5%, we'll pin canary back and roll to stable. Prepare rollback cmd: `deploy rollback --deployment c-3178901234 --to runtime=2.3.0 --config=stable`.

Rae: 21:25 checks: 401s settled after proxy cache purge. p95 still +20ms. No action.

Samir: Proceeding with full rollout to 50% in 5m per schedule.

deploy-bot: Rollforward to 50% at 21:31 UTC. All health checks passing. Note: change footnote in release notes: 'reduced per-user rate limit, tighter batching for cost savings; careful monitoring for auth cache effects.'

Jules: Tagged release notes draft: 'service-config: rate/batch/ttl adjust — perf tradeoffs tested in canary.' I'll post in #eng-releases channel and product afterwards.

Maya: Leaving a final note — if customers report increased p95, revert batch_window_ms to 12 and bump kv_cache_ttl back to 600.

Samir: Ack. Closing thread once we hit 50% stable for 30m. :eyes:

Rae: :+1:
